output.title: Decreasing Students’ Stress Through Time Management Training

scenes.narration: This paper asks a practical question: can a short time management training reduce undergraduate students’ perceived stress and increase perceived control of time?
scenes.layout_description: A single student sits between a tangled clock and a calmer calendar, with orange arrows pointing toward order.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal hand-drawn black ink line art on solid cream background: a worried student at a desk, a messy clock on one side, an organized calendar on the other, orange arrow connecting them, yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: The authors begin from prior work describing university student mental health as an increasing concern, with stress linked to difficulties in study.
scenes.layout_description: A student silhouette carries a backpack filled with small books and a heavy stress cloud above it.
scenes.visual_prompt: Sketch-like black ink illustration on cream: student walking under a large cloud labeled with simple hand text, books spilling from backpack, orange circle around the cloud, yellow accents.

scenes.narration: They cite Pierceall and Keim, where 75 % of 212 community college students reported at least moderate stress, and 13 % high stress levels.
scenes.layout_description: Two simple groups of student figures are shown beside a small cited-study clipboard.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink on cream: clipboard marked cited study, rows of small student icons, orange brackets highlighting a large group and a smaller group, yellow dots for emphasis.

scenes.narration: Prior studies cited in the paper point to time-related demands, including workload, time pressure and self-organized learning, as serious student problems for students.
scenes.layout_description: Three icons surround one student: a book pile, a ticking clock, and an open planner.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink drawing on cream: student in center, heavy stack of books, clock with orange alarm marks, open planner with yellow highlight, simple arrows toward student.

scenes.narration: Time management interventions are recommended in student support, but the authors stress that evidence on their effectiveness for students is still scarce.
scenes.layout_description: A help desk offers a small planner, while a thin evidence stack sits beside it.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn cream background: support desk, student reaching for planner, tiny stack of papers labeled scarce evidence, orange question mark, yellow underline.

scenes.narration: A previous Häfner et al. study found stress did not rise after training, but it did not show a decrease in stress.
scenes.layout_description: A flat stress line is drawn on a chart, with a missing downward arrow shown faintly.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink sketch on cream: simple chart with horizontal line, student looking at it, orange crossed-out downward arrow, yellow highlight on flat line.

scenes.narration: Here, the authors wanted to test whether training could increase perceived control of time and decrease tension, with two follow-up measurements afterward.
scenes.layout_description: A timeline shows before training, then two later checkpoints with opposite arrows for control and tension.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal ink line art: horizontal timeline, training marker in orange, two checkpoint circles, upward arrow over small clock, downward arrow over stress cloud, yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: They describe effective time management as time assessment, goal setting, planning and monitoring, following Häfner and Stock’s earlier description of the concept.
scenes.layout_description: Four small tiles form a simple process path from looking at time to checking progress.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink on cream: four connected tiles with icons of clock, target, calendar, checklist; orange arrows between tiles; yellow accents.

scenes.narration: The study used a non-equivalent dependent variable design: one trained group, expected outcome variables, and demands as a control variable for comparison.
scenes.layout_description: One group of students branches into three measurement cards, with demands set apart as comparison.
scenes.visual_prompt: Sketch-like black ink: single circle of students, three cards labeled with short words, orange branch arrows, demands card outlined in yellow.

scenes.narration: The logic was that stress and control should change after training, while perceived, self-reported demands should not change because of training itself.
scenes.layout_description: Two gauges move after training while a third gauge stays level.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink on cream: three simple dial gauges, first two with orange moving needles, third with steady yellow baseline, small training icon nearby.

scenes.narration: In supporting this design, the paper quotes Frese et al., who argued it can help rule out testing and nonspecific placebo effects.
scenes.layout_description: A quotation bubble hovers over a shield blocking two small threat icons.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink: quote bubble attributed Frese et al., shield in center, two small arrows labeled testing and placebo stopped by shield, orange and yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: The initial sample was 48 local undergraduate students from a medium-sized German university, recruited through boards, newsletters and seminar invitations to participate.
scenes.layout_description: A campus notice board, newsletter sheet, and seminar doorway point toward a student group.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink sketch on cream: university building, notice board, paper newsletter, classroom door, arrows leading to a group of students, orange circles around recruitment sources.

scenes.narration: For the main analyses, the authors used data from 23 participants who completed questionnaires before training, 2 weeks after, and 4 weeks after.
scenes.layout_description: Twenty-three simple dots sit below three questionnaire checkpoints on a timeline.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal ink illustration: timeline with three clipboard icons, dots representing participants, orange highlight at training start, yellow circles at 2 weeks and 4 weeks.

scenes.narration: These 23 students had a mean age of 23.30 years, SD=2.80, studied different subjects, and about half were female, 52 %, in this sample.
scenes.layout_description: A mixed student group is surrounded by small subject icons and a simple age card.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink on cream: diverse group of students, small icons for subjects like book, atom, scales, computer; age card highlighted orange, yellow circle around group.

scenes.narration: The training lasted for 4 h, was extracurricular, carried no incentives, and was held in groups of about ten students by one trainer.
scenes.layout_description: A trainer stands beside a small seated group and a clock showing a highlighted training block.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink drawing: one trainer at flip chart, about ten student figures seated, clock with orange segment, small empty gift box crossed out, yellow accents.

scenes.narration: Training began with students reflecting on current academic and extracurricular activities, then identifying which activities were most important for their study goals.
scenes.layout_description: A student sorts activity cards into a highlighted important pile beside a target.
scenes.visual_prompt: Sketch-like ink art on cream: student at desk with cards showing book, sport, club, study; orange arrow sorting to target; yellow highlight on important pile.

scenes.narration: Next, they defined concrete, challenging and proximal goals, set deadlines, developed steps toward goals, prioritized steps, and considered obstacles and responses to them.
scenes.layout_description: A staircase leads to a target, with deadline flags and an obstacle marked by a detour arrow.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink: steps ascending toward target, small flags for deadlines, rock obstacle on step, orange detour arrow, yellow highlight on goal.

scenes.narration: The final parts focused on daily planning, deciding what to do and when, avoiding distractions, and monitoring which tasks were completed daily.
scenes.layout_description: A daily schedule and checklist sit beside a muted distraction icon.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal cream background: open day planner, checklist with ticks, phone or distraction icon pushed aside, orange schedule blocks, yellow check marks.

scenes.narration: Time management behaviour was measured with 18 items; perceived control of time used ten items from an adapted Time Management Behavior Scale.
scenes.layout_description: Two questionnaire sheets are shown, one for behaviour and one for control of time.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink sketch: two clipboards with checkboxes, one with many small boxes, one beside a clock icon, orange bracket around 18 items, yellow highlight near control clock.

scenes.narration: Perceived stress was measured with the five-item tension scale, covering mental fatigue, trouble relaxing and nervousness, using a 1 to 5 range.
scenes.layout_description: A tension questionnaire card sits next to simple icons for fatigue, relaxing trouble, and nervousness.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink on cream: clipboard labeled tension scale, tired face, tangled resting chair, shaky lines near hands, orange 1-to-5 scale, yellow accents.

scenes.narration: Demands, the control variable, used five items about the amount of work and external duties, also with a 1 to 5 range.
scenes.layout_description: A demands questionnaire is paired with a book pile and outside-duty checklist.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal ink line art: clipboard for demands, stack of work papers, separate duties list, orange underline on control variable, yellow 1-to-5 scale.

scenes.narration: After training, reported use of taught strategies showed a nearly significant increase at 2 weeks, and a significant increase at 4 weeks.
scenes.layout_description: A rising strategy-use line has a small lift at 2 weeks and a clearer lift at 4 weeks.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn chart on cream: line rising gently then more clearly, two time points circled, tiny planner icon, orange arrow upward, yellow highlight at final point.

scenes.narration: In the repeated-measurement MANOVA, trainees reported significantly less tension 2 weeks after training than before training, F(1,22)=8.22, p<0.01, for the perceived stress outcome.
scenes.layout_description: A before-and-after tension meter drops from high to lower at the 2-week mark.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink: two vertical meters labeled before and 2 weeks, stress cloud shrinking, orange downward arrow, yellow circle around lower meter.

scenes.narration: For perceived control of time, 2 weeks showed only a tendency in the expected direction; at 4 weeks, the increase was significant.
scenes.layout_description: A control-of-time line rises slightly at 2 weeks and more clearly at 4 weeks.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn cream scene: clock with reins or handle, line graph rising from before to 2 weeks to 4 weeks, orange small arrow then larger arrow, yellow highlight at 4 weeks.

scenes.narration: At 4 weeks, participants also reported less tension than before training, with a significant time effect, F(1,22)=5.75, p=0.03, for perceived stress outcome.
scenes.layout_description: A 4-week checkpoint shows the tension cloud smaller than at the starting point.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink illustration: timeline from before to 4 weeks, large cloud at start and smaller cloud at end, orange downward arrow, yellow ring around 4-week checkpoint.

scenes.narration: Demands did not change significantly at either follow-up, and reported effects were stronger for students with no or little prior time-management experience.
scenes.layout_description: A steady demands line is shown beside two student groups, with the no-experience group highlighted.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal sketch: flat demands line across timeline, two small groups of students, group labeled no or little circled in orange, yellow emphasis arrows toward larger effect marks.

scenes.narration: The authors conclude time management training might benefit undergraduate well-being, but larger samples and further intervention studies are needed for robust conclusions.
scenes.layout_description: A cautious takeaway card shows a small positive sign beside a larger future research path.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink on cream: open paper with takeaway note, small student smiling beside planner, long path of future study papers ahead, orange cautious arrow, yellow highlight.
